title: Build List Keys
prompt: A React list needs stable keys for rendered rows. Write a helper that returns each item id as a string. If an item has no id, use "fallback-" followed by its index.

explanation.beginner: Start by identifying what the function receives and what it must return. For Build List Keys, read the story as a simple input-to-output rule: A React list needs stable keys for rendered rows. Write a helper that returns each item id as a string. If an item has no id, use "fallback-" followed by its index. Work through one small example by hand, then write the steps in React using plain variables before worrying about making the code shorter.
explanation.junior: Treat this as a small pure React function: avoid mutating inputs unless the prompt explicitly asks for it, return the requested shape exactly, and let the tests drive the edge cases. The main practice area is react, lists and keys. Pay attention to edge cases and keep the transformation predictable as the input grows.
